# Nonrigid sectors and q-Fock locality

## Result

**The positive full-Fock/infinite-statistics route has a direct observable-locality obstruction, not just a missing antiparticle cup.** In the norm-closed algebra generated by bounded q-creation operators, with real |q|<1 and mixing one-particle spatial translations, every bounded-region local observable has zero vacuum variance. The resulting observable vacuum GNS representation is one-dimensional. This statement includes arbitrary norm-convergent observables, not only fields or quadratic densities.

There are two essential qualifications. First, the full Boltzmann Fock space (q=0) is not the finite-internal-label R=I Fock construction of the earlier notes. Second, a fresh observable net in the **strong closure** is not excluded: the strong closure is all bounded operators. In fact the vacuum projection has exact norm distance 1/2 from the creation C*-algebra. Strongly dressed observables are a real change of assumptions, not something already covered by norm approximation.

A separate literature check makes the massive nonrigid route more restrictive. In the irreducible massive-sector AQFT setting with the relevant duality assumptions, existence of an isolated positive mass shell implies finite statistics and a conjugate. Finite one-particle multiplicity is not the hypothesis responsible for that particular conclusion in the precise restatement checked below. This is not a theorem from observable locality, positivity and covariance alone, and cone-localized field reconstruction is not a complete bounded-region field reconstruction.

No interacting model with the requested new involutive physical statistics has been constructed.

## 1. Objects and the distinction from finite R

Use Minkowski signature (+,-,...,-), hbar=c=1, spatial dimension s>=1, mass mu>0, and

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal H_1&=L^2\left(\mathbb R^s,\frac{d^sp}{2\omega_{\mathbf p}}\right)\otimes V,
&\omega_{\mathbf p}&=\sqrt{\mathbf p^2+\mu^2},\\
(u(\mathbf a)f)(\mathbf p)&=e^{-i\mathbf p\cdot\mathbf a}f(\mathbf p).
\end{aligned}
$$

The inner product is antilinear in its first argument. Finite-dimensional V suffices; the argument also permits a separable internal space whenever the stated weak mixing holds. Here mixing means pointwise decay of matrix coefficients, not merely a Cesaro condition. The proof below needs only

$$
\langle f,u(\mathbf a)g\rangle\longrightarrow0\qquad(|\mathbf a|\longrightarrow\infty).
$$

For this mass-shell representation it follows from Cauchy-Schwarz and the Riemann-Lebesgue lemma. The mass gap, time evolution, Lorentz transformations and finite internal dimension are not used in the algebraic obstruction once this property is established.

For real |q|<1, let F_q(H_1) be q-Fock space: its n-particle algebraic space is H_1^{tensor n}, with inner product

$$
\langle \xi,\eta\rangle_q
=\langle\xi,P_{q,n}\eta\rangle,
\qquad
P_{q,n}=\sum_{\pi\in S_n}q^{\operatorname{inv}(\pi)}U(\pi).
$$

Here U(pi) is the ordinary tensor-permutation operator before q-deformation, and Omega is the unit vector in the zero-particle space. These forms are positive definite. Left creation is a_q^dagger(f) xi=f tensor xi; its adjoint obeys

$$
a_q(f)a_q^\dagger(g)-q a_q^\dagger(g)a_q(f)=\langle f,g\rangle I,
\qquad
\|a_q^\dagger(f)\|\leq\frac{\|f\|}{\sqrt{1-|q|}}.
$$

Define

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal E_q&=C^*(I,a_q^\dagger(f):f\in\mathcal H_1),\\
\alpha_{\mathbf a}&=\operatorname{Ad}\Gamma_q(u(\mathbf a)),
&\omega(A)&=\langle\Omega,A\Omega\rangle.
\end{aligned}
$$

The closure in E_q is the **operator norm** closure. At q=0 this is the full unsymmetrized Fock construction and a(f)a^dagger(g)=<f,g>I. Positivity of q-Fock space does not itself provide a local observable net or identify a physical charge category.

Write h_mu for the orbital L^2 factor above. In contrast, if the exchange in the earlier finite-R convention swaps orbital factors and acts as R=I on V tensor V, then

$$
\mathcal F_{R,n}\simeq\operatorname{Sym}^n(h_\mu)\otimes V^{\otimes n},
\qquad
\mathcal F_{0,n}=(h_\mu\otimes V)^{\otimes n}.
$$

With d orbital modes and m=dim V the dimensions are respectively m^n binomial(n+d-1,n) and (md)^n. For m=2,d=3, n=0,...,4 they are (1,6,24,80,240) and (1,6,36,216,1296). Their one-orbital-mode counting coincides, but their multimode spaces do not. The theorem below must not be transferred to finite R=I by that counting coincidence. Also T=q times the flip is a Fock twist, not an involutive unitary exchange when |q|<1.

## 2. Exact translation-limit theorem

Let Pi_n denote the orthogonal n-particle projection, and set

$$
x_n=\Pi_n(A-\omega(A)I)\Omega,
\qquad
y_m=\Pi_m(B-\omega(B)I)\Omega.
$$

**Theorem.** For arbitrary A,B in E_q,

$$
\boxed{
\lim_{|\mathbf a|\to\infty}
\|[A,\alpha_{\mathbf a}(B)]\Omega\|_q^2
=2\sum_{n,m\geq1}(1-q^{nm})\|x_n\|_q^2\|y_m\|_q^2.
}\tag{1}
$$

In particular, writing Var(A)=||(A-omega(A)I)Omega||_q^2,

$$
\lim_{|\mathbf a|\to\infty}\|[A,\alpha_{\mathbf a}(B)]\Omega\|_q^2
\geq2c(q)\operatorname{Var}(A)\operatorname{Var}(B),
\qquad
c(q)=\begin{cases}1-q,&0\leq q<1,\\1-q^2,&-1<q<0.\end{cases}\tag{2}
$$

This coefficient is sharp for unrestricted pairs A,B: use particle degrees (1,1) for q>=0 and (1,2) for q<0. For q=0 the right side of (1) is exactly 2 Var(A) Var(B).

### Proof

First consider finite polynomials with one-particle supports in orthogonal finite-dimensional subspaces K and L. Normal ordering uses only the q-CCR above. Each centered polynomial is a sum of normal words (creators followed by annihilators), with zero constant term. On a word entirely from the other support, every term containing an annihilator vanishes. Consequently, on the vacuum,

$$
(A-\omega(A)I)(B-\omega(B)I)\Omega
=\sum_{n,m\geq1}x_n\otimes y_m,
$$

and the reversed product is the sum of y_m tensor x_n.

In the q-Gram form, permutations that contribute to these inner products must preserve the two support labels. Permutations within each block give its q-norm. Moving an n-block through an m-block introduces exactly nm inversions. Thus

$$
\begin{aligned}
\|x_n\otimes y_m\|_q^2
&=\|x_n\|_q^2\|y_m\|_q^2,\\
\langle x_n\otimes y_m,y_m\otimes x_n\rangle_q
&=q^{nm}\|x_n\|_q^2\|y_m\|_q^2.
\end{aligned}
$$

Terms with different (n,m) are orthogonal by their occupation numbers in K and L. This proves (1) in the exactly orthogonal-support case.

For finite polynomial supports K and u(a)L, all cross Gram entries tend to zero by weak mixing. Equivalently one can orthogonalize u(a)L against K with a change of its finitely many generators tending to zero. Boundedness and norm continuity of the creators make the polynomial calculation converge to the orthogonal-support result.

Finally approximate A,B in operator norm. The commutator norm on the left is uniformly continuous in A,B, independently of a, since alpha_a is isometric. On the right, norm convergence of centered vacuum vectors gives l^1 convergence of their squared particle-component norms; the coefficients 1-q^{nm} lie between 0 and 2. Thus both sides converge and the formula extends to E_q. Taking the minimum of 1-q^{nm} over positive n,m proves (2). This is an analytic all-particle-number proof, not an inference from the finite checks. QED.

## 3. Consequence for observable locality

Suppose O maps to A(O) is an isotonic translation-covariant net of bounded observable algebras contained in E_q. Assume ordinary, ungraded spacelike commutativity. For bounded O, O and O+a are spacelike separated for sufficiently large purely spatial a. Taking B=A in (2) therefore gives

$$
A\Omega=\omega(A)\Omega
\qquad(A\in\mathcal A(O)).\tag{3}
$$

This conclusion holds for A and A^dagger, so every local algebra reduces the line C Omega. The restriction of omega to the generated observable algebra is a character; its GNS Hilbert space is one-dimensional. Nontrivial vacuum cyclicity is impossible in this class. If Omega is separating for each local algebra, those algebras themselves are scalar.

Without the separating property, (3) does **not** say every represented operator is scalar: operators can act on states invisible from the vacuum. Faithfulness of the Fock representation of E_q is not faithfulness of its vacuum state. The theorem rules out a nontrivial observable vacuum theory, not every operator-valued family without that requirement.

This uses no DHR criterion, no crossing relation, no finite statistical dimension and no spacelike commutativity of the charged generators. It addresses the observables directly. It also applies to an interacting theory expressed on a q-Fock scattering space if its spatial translations have the specified second-quantized form **and** its actual local bounded observables belong to E_q. The last condition is substantial and has not been derived from asymptotic completeness.

At the formal q=1 endpoint the coefficient in (1) disappears; bosonic creators are then unbounded, so the norm-algebra setup changes. At q=-1 only odd-odd degrees survive, giving 4||x_odd||^2||y_odd||^2. Even CAR observables escape the obstruction, consistently with ordinary fermionic locality. These limits are checks, not a claim that all endpoint operator algebras are identical.

## 4. Explicit neutral-pair witness

Give two internal labels charges +1 and -1 under a global U(1). For orthonormal modes p_X,a_X,p_Y,a_Y, define bounded neutral operators

$$
A_X=a_q^\dagger(p_X)a_q^\dagger(a_X)+a_q(a_X)a_q(p_X),
\qquad A_Y\text{ analogously}.
$$

Then

$$
[A_X,A_Y]\Omega
=|p_X,a_X,p_Y,a_Y\rangle-|p_Y,a_Y,p_X,a_X\rangle,
\qquad
\|[A_X,A_Y]\Omega\|_q^2=2(1-q^4).\tag{4}
$$

Thus charge neutrality does not restore commutativity. Number-preserving quadratic densities cannot cancel this four-particle component. More generally at q=0, for arbitrary two-particle neutral kernels F,G and number-preserving additions D_F,D_G,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Pi_4[A_F,A_G]\Omega&=F\otimes G-G\otimes F,\\
\|\Pi_4[A_F,A_G]\Omega\|^2
&=2\bigl(\|F\|^2\|G\|^2-|\langle F,G\rangle|^2\bigr),
\end{aligned}
$$

where A_F=L^dagger(F)+L(F)+D_F and L^dagger(F) concatenates the pair F on the left.

Orthogonality of modes is not being identified with compact spacetime localization. The actual large-separation test can be made explicit. In one spatial dimension choose width sigma>0 and the normalized orbital packet

$$
f(p)=\left(\frac{\sigma}{\sqrt\pi}\right)^{1/2}\sqrt{2\omega_p}\,e^{-\sigma^2p^2/2},
\qquad \langle f,u(L)f\rangle=e^{-L^2/(4\sigma^2)}=:c_L.
$$

Use this packet in both charge labels and translate the second pair by L. The real overlaps make the vacuum component of the commutator cancel, and exact q-Gram contraction gives

$$
\|[A_0,A_L]\Omega\|_q^2
=2(1-q^4)(1-c_L^4)
=2(1-q^4)(1-e^{-L^2/\sigma^2}).\tag{5}
$$

The Gaussian itself is not compactly supported. Equation (5) proves these operators cannot be assigned bounded localization while retaining the specified translations: the commutator tends to a nonzero constant rather than becoming zero. The general theorem supplies the statement for every norm-limit observable, independent of this packet choice.

## 5. The strong-closure boundary is sharp

For infinite-dimensional H_1 and every |q|<1,

$$
\mathcal E_q''=B(\mathcal F_q),
\qquad
\boxed{\operatorname{dist}(P_\Omega,\mathcal E_q)=\frac12.}\tag{6}
$$

For the first equality, an operator commuting with all creators and annihilators must send Omega into the common annihilator kernel C Omega, then act as the same scalar on the dense creator orbit. Thus E_q has scalar commutant.

For the distance statement choose a countable orthonormal basis e_j of H_1. Normal ordering shows

$$
\langle e_j,Ae_j\rangle\longrightarrow\omega(A)
\qquad(A\in\mathcal E_q).
$$

Indeed, apart from the scalar term, only a normal word with one creator and one annihilator can contribute to the one-particle diagonal; its contribution tends to zero. Extend from polynomials by norm approximation. If r=||P_Omega-A||, the vacuum and these one-particle states imply |1-omega(A)|<=r and |omega(A)|<=r. Hence r>=1/2, attained by A=I/2.

At q=0 the strong approximation is particularly explicit:

$$
P_\Omega=\mathrm{s}\!\!\lim_{N\to\infty}
\left(I-\sum_{j=1}^N a_0^\dagger(e_j)a_0(e_j)\right).
$$

Each difference from P_Omega has norm one. Creator-P_Omega-annihilator products then produce rank-one matrix units. For normalized one-particle F, the rank-one dressed field A_F=|F><Omega|+|Omega><F| already invalidates the norm-algebra translation-limit formula: its variance is one, but [A_F,alpha_a(A_F)]Omega=2i Im<F,u(a)F> Omega tends to zero. It does not satisfy local commutativity on excited states.

Two operations must be separated. Taking strong closures of an **already local** net satisfying (3) cannot restore vacuum excitations, because the reducing line persists. Defining a **different** net inside E_q'' is not covered. Doing so must actually prove covariance, locality, nontrivial vacuum representation, the physical charged sectors, interaction and the required comparison with ordinary fields. E_q''=B(F_q) alone supplies none of these.

### What existing twisted-Araki-Woods results do and do not settle

[Correa da Silva–Lechner, arXiv:2212.02298v2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2212.02298v2) gives two complementary results, whose relevant pages were visually checked:

- **Theorem 4.9, PDF/printed p.34:** a compatible half-sided modular inclusion L_T(U(1)H) subset L_T(H), with a braided crossing-symmetric twist ||T||<1, has trivial relative commutant. Their section 5, p.41, applies this to lightlike wedge translations and intervals on a lightray. This excludes the corresponding null-localized observables. It is not, by itself, a theorem that every open massive double-cone intersection is trivial.
- **Proposition 4.11, p.36, with applications p.42:** if K subset H are standard subspaces, T is braided, compatible with both, crossing-symmetric for H, ||T||<1, and ||Delta_H^{1/4} Delta_K^{-1/4}||_1<1, the inclusion is quasi-split. When the larger algebra is type III, the relative commutant is type III. In suitable massless double-cone inclusions this produces many operators commuting with the inner algebra. It does not construct a full relativistic local net with new statistics; the paper explicitly distinguishes this geometry from the wedge-local construction.

These results prevent both overstatements: neither “positive quon fields automatically give local observables” nor “every strong completion has already been ruled out” is justified.

## 6. Massive nonrigid sectors: the actual theorem input

Here the statistical dimension is that of an **irreducible physical charge sector**, not the number of internal labels or the size of a direct sum. Let M_chi=(P_chi^2)^{1/2} be the sector's positive mass operator.

[Mund, arXiv:0801.3621v2, PDF/printed p.6](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0801.3621v2#page=6) separates:

1. (A1) m>0;
2. (A2) m is isolated in the spectrum of M_chi;
3. (A3) the corresponding one-particle Poincare representation is a finite multiple of one mass-spin representation.

The paragraph following these assumptions explicitly states that **A1 and A2**, together with the standard observable assumptions and weak duality, provide cone localization and exclude infinite statistics lambda=0. [Appendix A, p.16](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0801.3621v2#page=16) states the existence of a conjugate cone-localized morphism. This is a precise restatement of the Fredenhagen/Buchholz–Fredenhagen input, not a new proof here. A3 is used for Mund's stronger spin-statistics and particle-antiparticle multiplicity conclusions. Therefore simply allowing infinite shell degeneracy is not an established way around this particular finite-statistics theorem.

For a sufficient explicit observable hypothesis package, rather than silently assuming minimal weak duality, [Mund, arXiv:0902.4434v2, pp.5–7, Eqs. (7)–(10)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0902.4434v2#page=5) uses:

- an isotonic local observable net with positive-energy Poincare covariance;
- a unique invariant vacuum, Reeh–Schlieder, and an irreducible vacuum net;
- Haag duality A_0(I')=A_0(I)' for spacelike cones, their complements and wedges;
- irreducible positive-energy covariant sectors, represented by localized transportable cone morphisms.

Its p.7 records finite statistics and conjugates as consequences of the massive input. Its later BW/CPT theorem additionally uses the stronger full mass hypothesis and asymptotic completeness; those later assumptions must not be retroactively described as necessary for the narrower 0801.3621 statement. No split or nuclearity hypothesis is being added to the finite-statistics statement here. The original 1981/1982 PDFs could not be independently reread; no original theorem number or minimality claim is asserted on the basis of their abstracts.

Mund's setting is 2+1 dimensional, where cone charges may braid. In the 3+1-dimensional BF setting the charge exchange is symmetric, so finite statistics leads to ordinary Bose/Fermi categorical reconstruction. This does not turn a cone-localized field system into a complete **bounded-region** field system. The [complete-field-net comparison](<Complete field nets and R-parastatistics.md>) remains a separate requirement. No conclusion here rules out all 1+1-dimensional kink/soliton settings or derives these duality assumptions from the three minimal observable axioms.

### Why irreducibility cannot be dropped

An ordinary control is the U(1)-fixed observable net of a free massive complex scalar. Each integer charge-n sector pi_n is irreducible with d(pi_n)=1. The countable direct sum

$$
\pi=\bigoplus_{n\geq1}\pi_n
$$

has infinite total dimension and no finite rigid conjugate, but contains the isolated scalar mass-mu shell of multiplicity one from pi_1. The charge-n threshold is n mu, so the other summands begin at 2 mu or higher. This is not an irreducible sector: its observable von Neumann algebra has a nontrivial center. Every constituent and the original field realization are ordinary. Thus “every object containing an isolated shell is rigid” would be false.

Genuinely irreducible nonrigid chiral sectors are already recorded in the [Virasoro/current control](<R-parastatistics and local relativistic interactions.md#L699-L716>). They have positive conformal energy but not an isolated positive Poincare mass shell; they do not provide the requested new massive permutation statistics or inequivalence to an ordinary parent.

## 7. Research boundary

The nonrigid escape now has two explicit tests rather than an unspecified failure of DR:

1. For a full/q-Fock construction with mixing translations, a nontrivial local vacuum observable cannot be a norm-limit of the bounded creation polynomials. A viable construction must supply genuinely different strong-limit/dressed observables or a different representation and prove their local algebra.
2. For an irreducible charged sector with an isolated positive mass shell, the applicable cone-localization and duality hypotheses must be checked. If they hold, invoking infinite statistical dimension is unavailable. If they fail, that failure must be exhibited in the actual observable theory; it is not established by unusual Fock counting.

A concrete next construction test is a non-norm-polynomial local observable algebra in a positive gapless or nonisolated-mass representation, followed by an intrinsic charge-exchange calculation. The existing strong relative-commutant results supply possible operator-algebraic ingredients but not yet such a model. Changing q or calling the auxiliary twist a physical permutation operator does not complete the original goal.

**Assumptions:** q-Fock positivity and its bounded creator estimate; pointwise mixing spatial translations; ordinary locality of bounded observables; the norm-algebra hypothesis for sections 2–4. Massive-sector finite-statistics results and modular-inclusion results are explicit literature inputs with their additional hypotheses, not consequences of the original three axioms.

**Not verified:** A nontrivial interacting local net in the surviving strong/gapless class; its physical nonrigid charge structure or new involutive statistics; exclusion of all complete ordinary parents; the minimal original 1981/1982 theorem hypotheses; or a universal no-go. The original construction objective remains open.
